{{inline |date=May 2024}}
The '''Hecke algebra of a finite group''' is the [[algebra over a field|algebra]] spanned by the [[double coset]]s ''HgH'' of a [[subgroup]] ''H'' of a [[finite group]] ''G''. It is a special case of a [[Hecke algebra of a locally compact group]].

== Definition ==
Let ''F'' be a [[field (mathematics)|field]] of [[characteristic (algebra)|characteristic]] zero, ''G'' a finite [[group (mathematics)|group]] and ''H'' a subgroup of ''G''. Let <math>F[G]</math> denote the
[[group ring|group algebra]] of ''G'': the space of ''F''-valued functions on ''G'' with the multiplication given by convolution. We write <math>F[G/H]</math> for the space of ''F''-valued functions on <math>G/H</math>. An (''F''-valued) function on ''G''/''H'' determines and is determined by a function on ''G'' that is invariant under the right action of ''H''. That is, there is the natural identification:
:<math>F[G/H] = F[G]^H.</math>
Similarly, there is the identification
:<math>R := \operatorname{End}_G(F[G/H]) = F[G]^{H \times H}</math>
given by sending a ''G''-linear map ''f'' to the value of ''f'' evaluated at the characteristic function of ''H''. For each double coset <math>HgH</math>, let <math>T_g</math> denote the characteristic function of it. Then those <math>T_g</math>'s form a [[basis (linear algebra)|basis]] of ''R''.

== Application in representation theory ==
Let <math>\varphi : G \rightarrow GL(V)</math> be any finite-dimensional [[complex number|complex]] [[representation of a finite group|representation]] of a finite group ''G'', the Hecke algebra <math>H = \operatorname{End}_G(V)</math> is the algebra of ''G''-[[Representation theory#Equivariant maps and isomorphisms|equivariant]] [[Endomorphism|endomorphisms]] of ''V''. For each [[irreducible representation]] <math>W</math> of ''G'', the [[Group action|action]] of ''H'' on ''V'' preserves <math>\tilde{W}</math> – the [[isotypic component]] of <math>W</math> – and commutes with <math>W</math> as a ''G'' action.
